title: Count connected components
prompt: n nodes are numbered 0..n-1; edges is a list of undirected [a, b] pairs. Return the number of connected components.
hints: Build an adjacency list.
Start a traversal from every unvisited node and count the starts.
Mark nodes when you first see them.

title: Course order (Kahn)
prompt: Courses 0..n-1; prereqs is a list of [course, required] pairs. Return an order to take all courses where the smallest available course number is always taken next, or [] if impossible.
hints: Edge required → course; count in-degrees.
A heap of courses with in-degree 0 gives the smallest-first rule.
If you output fewer than n courses, there's a cycle.

title: Shortest path in a grid
prompt: grid is a list of strings with '.' open and '#' blocked. Return the fewest moves (up/down/left/right) from the top-left to the bottom-right cell, or -1 if unreachable or if either cell is blocked.
hints: Unit-cost moves: BFS gives shortest paths.
Store distance per cell when first discovered.
Check bounds and walls before enqueueing.

title: Does a directed graph have a cycle?
prompt: Nodes 0..n-1, directed edges [a, b] meaning a → b. Return True if the graph contains a directed cycle.
hints: Kahn's algorithm outputs every node exactly when there's no cycle.
Alternatively DFS with three colours: white, grey (on the stack), black.
A grey-to-grey edge is a cycle.

title: Union–find: count groups after merges
prompt: n items start in their own groups. Apply every union [a, b] in order and return the number of groups.
hints: parent[x] = x at first.
find walks to the root (compress the path as you go).
Each union of two different roots reduces the group count by one.

title: Dijkstra distances
prompt: n nodes 0..n-1, directed weighted edges [a, b, w] with w >= 0. Return the list of shortest distances from source, with -1 for unreachable nodes.
hints: Pop the closest unsettled node from a heap.
Skip entries whose distance is larger than the best known.
Relax each outgoing edge.

title: Minimum spanning tree cost
prompt: n nodes 0..n-1 and undirected weighted edges [a, b, w]. Return the total weight of a minimum spanning tree, or -1 if the graph is not connected.
hints: Sort edges by weight (Kruskal).
Add an edge if it joins two different components (union–find).
A spanning tree has exactly n − 1 edges.

title: First redundant connection
prompt: Edges [a, b] are added one by one to an undirected graph of nodes 1..n. Return the first edge that connects two nodes already connected, or [] if none does.
hints: Union–find tells whether two nodes are already connected.
Size the parent array from the largest node label.
Return the edge whose endpoints have the same root.

title: House robber
prompt: Return the maximum sum of non-adjacent values in nums (values >= 0; 0 for an empty list).
hints: At each house: take it plus the best two back, or skip it.
best(i) = max(best(i-1), best(i-2) + nums[i]).
Keep two rolling values.

title: Fewest coins
prompt: Return the fewest coins (unlimited supply of each denomination) that sum to amount, or -1 if impossible. amount >= 0.
hints: best[a] = fewest coins for amount a; best[0] = 0.
best[a] = 1 + min(best[a - c]) over coins c <= a.
Use infinity for impossible amounts.

title: Longest common subsequence
prompt: Return the length of the longest subsequence common to strings a and b.
hints: dp[i][j] = LCS length of a[:i] and b[:j].
Equal last characters extend dp[i-1][j-1].
Otherwise take max(dp[i-1][j], dp[i][j-1]).

title: Decode ways
prompt: A message of digits maps 'A'=1 … 'Z'=26. Return how many ways s can be decoded (an empty string has 1 way; a leading zero makes a part invalid).
hints: dp[i] = ways to decode s[:i]; dp[0] = 1.
One digit s[i-1] counts if it's not '0'.
Two digits s[i-2:i] count if they form 10..26.

title: Word search in a grid
prompt: board is a list of strings. Return True if word can be formed by adjacent (up/down/left/right) cells, using each cell at most once per path.
hints: Try every cell as a start.
Mark a cell as used during the recursion, then restore it.
Stop when all characters of word are matched.

title: Generate balanced parentheses
prompt: Return all strings of n pairs of balanced parentheses, in lexicographic order ('(' sorts before ')').
hints: Add '(' while fewer than n are open.
Add ')' only while closes < opens.
Trying '(' before ')' yields lexicographic order.

title: Median of two sorted lists
prompt: a and b are sorted and not both empty. Return their combined median as a float, in O(log(min(len(a), len(b)))) using a partition search.
hints: Binary search the cut position i in the shorter list; j is determined.
A valid cut has a[i-1] <= b[j] and b[j-1] <= a[i] (with ±inf at the edges).
Odd total: max of left halves; even: average of the middle two.

title: Palindrome partitions
prompt: Return every way to split s into substrings that are all palindromes, as lists of parts, in the order produced by trying shorter first parts first.
hints: Choose the first part s[:k] if it's a palindrome, then partition the rest.
Try k from 1 upwards for the required order.
An empty remainder completes one partition.

title: Bellman–Ford distances
prompt: n nodes, directed edges [a, b, w] (weights may be negative, no negative cycles). Return shortest distances from source, with None for unreachable nodes.
hints: Start with 0 for the source and infinity elsewhere.
Relax every edge n − 1 times.
Skip edges whose start is still unreachable.

title: Negative cycle detector
prompt: Return True if the directed graph (n nodes, edges [a, b, w]) has a negative-weight cycle reachable from node 0.
hints: Run n − 1 rounds of Bellman–Ford from node 0.
Then try one more relaxation pass.
Any further improvement means a negative cycle.

title: Cheapest flight with at most k stops
prompt: n cities, flights [a, b, price]. Return the cheapest price from src to dst using at most k intermediate stops, or -1.
signature: def solve(n, flights, src, dst, k):
hints: At most k stops means at most k + 1 edges.
Run k + 1 rounds of Bellman–Ford, relaxing from a copy of last round's distances.
The copy stops a single round from using more than one new edge.

title: Fewest edges or least cost?
prompt: n nodes, directed weighted edges [a, b, w] (w >= 0). Return [fewest_edges, least_cost] from 0 to n-1, using -1 for both if unreachable.
hints: Fewest edges ignores weights: BFS.
Least cost needs Dijkstra.
They can choose different paths; compute both.

title: Cycle check with DFS colours
prompt: Directed graph on nodes 0..n-1 with edges [a, b]. Return True if it contains a cycle, using DFS with three colours.
hints: 0 = unvisited, 1 = on the current path, 2 = finished.
Reaching a node with colour 1 means a cycle.
Colour 2 after all neighbours are done.

title: Topological order by DFS finish times
prompt: Return a topological order of the DAG (nodes 0..n-1, edges [a, b] meaning a before b) as the reverse of DFS finish order, visiting start nodes and neighbours in increasing order.
hints: A node finishes after all nodes it points to.
Reverse the finish order.
Sort adjacency lists for a deterministic result.

title: Number of strongly connected components
prompt: Return the number of strongly connected components of the directed graph on nodes 0..n-1 with edges [a, b].
hints: Kosaraju: record DFS finish order on the graph.
Reverse every edge.
DFS the reversed graph in decreasing finish order; each new start is a component.

title: Safe states
prompt: A node is safe if every path from it ends at a node with no outgoing edges (never reaching a cycle). Return the sorted list of safe nodes of the directed graph on 0..n-1.
hints: Nodes on or leading into cycles are unsafe.
Reverse the edges and run Kahn from terminal nodes.
Nodes whose out-degree drops to 0 are safe.

title: Grid paths around walls
prompt: grid is a list of strings ('.' open, '#' wall). Count right/down paths from top-left to bottom-right (0 if either end is a wall).
hints: dp[r][c] = paths into (r, c).
Paths come from above and from the left.
Walls have 0 paths.

title: Minimum path sum
prompt: grid is a list of rows of non-negative integers. Return the minimum sum of a right/down path from the top-left to the bottom-right.
hints: dp[r][c] = cheapest cost to reach (r, c).
It's grid[r][c] plus the cheaper of above and left.
Fill the first row and column first, or handle edges with infinity.

title: Edit distance
prompt: Return the minimum number of single-character insertions, deletions or substitutions to turn a into b.
hints: d(i, j) = cost for a[:i] → b[:j].
If the last characters match, d(i, j) = d(i-1, j-1).
Otherwise 1 + min(delete, insert, substitute); d(i, 0) = i, d(0, j) = j.

title: Longest palindromic subsequence
prompt: Return the length of the longest subsequence of s that reads the same forwards and backwards.
hints: Interval state: best[i][j] for s[i..j].
Equal ends add 2 to the inside interval; otherwise drop one end.
Iterate by increasing interval length (or i from the end).

title: 0/1 knapsack in one row
prompt: Return the maximum total value of items (each used at most once) with total weight <= cap.
hints: best[c] = best value with capacity c.
For each item, update capacities from high to low.
best[c] = max(best[c], best[c - w] + v).

title: Count coin combinations
prompt: Return the number of combinations (order doesn't matter) of coins (unlimited supply) that sum to amount.
hints: ways[0] = 1.
Loop coins on the outside so each combination is counted once.
For each coin, amounts upwards: ways[a] += ways[a - c].

title: Longest increasing subsequence (n log n)
prompt: Return the length of the longest strictly increasing subsequence of nums in O(n log n).
hints: Keep tails[k] = smallest tail of an increasing subsequence of length k+1.
bisect_left finds where x goes.
Append if it extends the longest, otherwise replace.

title: Partition into equal sums
prompt: Return True if nums (positive integers) can be split into two groups with equal sums.
hints: An odd total is impossible.
Look for a subset summing to total // 2 (0/1 reuse).
A boolean array, updated downwards, or a set of reachable sums.

title: Range sums with point updates
prompt: Start from values. ops is a list of ['add', i, delta] or ['sum', lo, hi] (half-open). Return the results of every 'sum' in order, using a Fenwick tree.
hints: Build the tree by adding each value.
prefix(i) sums values[0:i]; range = prefix(hi) − prefix(lo).
Internally use 1-based indexes: i += 1.

title: Range minimum queries
prompt: Return the minimum of data[lo:hi] for each [lo, hi] in queries (half-open, non-empty), using an iterative segment tree.
hints: Leaves live at t[n:]; internal node i = min of children 2i and 2i+1.
Walk lo and hi up the tree, taking nodes at odd boundaries.
Identity for min is infinity.

title: Count smaller numbers to the right
prompt: For each index i, return how many values to the right of i are strictly smaller than nums[i], in O(n log n).
hints: Process from right to left.
Compress values to ranks, and use a Fenwick tree of counts.
Query the count of ranks below the current one, then add it.

title: Which structure?
prompt: Return the simplest suitable structure for the operation mix: 'prefix sums' if there are no updates, 'fenwick' for updates with an invertible combine (sum/xor), and 'segment tree' otherwise (min/max/gcd).
hints: No updates: precompute once.
Fenwick needs subtraction to answer ranges.
min, max and gcd can't be 'subtracted'.

title: Union by size: largest group
prompt: Apply the unions [a, b] to n singleton groups and return the size of the largest group.
hints: Keep size[root] for each root.
When merging, add the smaller size to the larger root.
Track the maximum size as you go (at least 1 when n > 0, 0 when n == 0).

title: Amortised cost of doubling
prompt: A dynamic array starts with capacity 1 and doubles when full. Return the total number of element copies caused by resizes while appending n elements (n >= 0).
hints: Each resize copies every current element.
Resizes happen when size reaches 1, 2, 4, 8, … and another append arrives.
Simulate: when size == capacity before an append, add size copies and double.

title: Accounts merge by shared email
prompt: Each account is [name, email1, email2, …]. Accounts sharing any email belong to the same person. Return merged accounts as [name, sorted emails…], sorted by their first email.
hints: Union the emails within each account.
Group emails by their root; remember a name per email.
Sort emails in each group, then sort the groups.

title: Rollback union–find
prompt: Process ops on n singletons: ['union', a, b], ['same', a, b] (record True/False), or ['undo'] (revert the most recent union that actually merged two sets; no-op if none). Return the recorded answers. Use union by size without path compression.
hints: Path compression would make undo impossible.
Push (child_root, parent_root) for each successful union.
Undo: pop, reset the child's parent and subtract its size.

title: A tiny differential tester
prompt: Return the list of inputs (from inputs) on which candidate(x) != oracle(x), where oracle sorts x and candidate is 'sorted unless the list has exactly 2 elements, then unchanged'.
hints: Write both functions inside solve.
Compare their outputs on every input.
Collect the disagreements in order.

title: Check a loop invariant
prompt: Run the max-finding loop on nums (non-empty) and return True if the invariant 'best == max(nums[:i])' holds before every iteration i from 1 to len(nums), and at the end.
hints: best starts as nums[0], so the invariant holds for i = 1.
Check the invariant at the top of each iteration.
After the loop, best should equal max(nums).

title: Find a counterexample to a greedy rule
prompt: The rule 'always take the largest coin that fits' is tested on amounts 1..limit. Return the list of all amounts where it uses more coins than optimal. coins contains 1.
hints: Compute optimal counts with a DP oracle.
Simulate the greedy rule.
Collect every amount where greedy is worse.

title: Metamorphic check for a sort
prompt: Given a list nums, return True if a sorting function passes three metamorphic checks on it: sorting is idempotent (sort(sort(x)) == sort(x)), length-preserving, and invariant to reversing the input. Use Python's sorted as the function.
hints: Compute s = sorted(nums) once.
Check each property with ==.
All three must hold.

title: Critical path length
prompt: tasks maps names to durations; deps is a list of [before, after]. With unlimited workers, return the time at which all tasks finish (the longest dependency path). The graph is a DAG.
hints: Process tasks in topological order.
finish[t] = duration[t] + max(finish of its prerequisites).
The answer is the maximum finish time (0 for no tasks).

title: Task order with priorities
prompt: Return a valid order of tasks respecting deps ([before, after]); whenever several tasks are ready, pick the one with the highest priority, then the smallest name. Return [] if there's a cycle.
hints: Kahn's algorithm with a heap of ready tasks.
Heap key: (-priority, name).
If fewer tasks are output than exist, report [].

title: Makespan with k workers
prompt: Independent tasks with the given durations are assigned in input order, each to the worker that becomes free earliest (ties: lowest worker id). Return the time when the last task finishes (0 for no tasks).
hints: A min-heap of (free_time, worker_id).
Pop the earliest-free worker, assign the next task, push back its new free time.
The answer is the largest finish time.

title: Deadline check
prompt: tasks maps names to durations, deps lists [before, after], and deadline is a number. With unlimited workers, return the sorted list of tasks whose earliest finish time exceeds deadline.
hints: Compute earliest finish times in topological order (critical path).
finish[t] = duration + max(finish of prerequisites).
Collect tasks with finish > deadline, sorted by name.
